answer: An orchard monitoring market could reward pigment measurements only when a randomly chosen fruit sample is checked by an independent lab. Allocate one fixed bounty per sample, so an agent swarm reporting it under many names cannot push verification costs to their nadir while multiplying rewards. To scale fraud, an attacker must acquire more samples or forge evidence that survives lab checks, paying collection and testing costs. Labs can collude and sample custody can fail; random lab rotation and auditable custody records reduce those risks without proving unique identities.
